messages:
kevin: Heads up — deploying release/2026.03.15 in the 22:00 UTC change window. Includes migration 2026_03_add_compound_index. Anyone seeing conflicts with active backfills?
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled by @kevin for 1750034567. Steps: apply-migration -> deploy services -> run-canary. Estimated lock: 3s per shard. Notify #eng-oncall if >5m lock.
maria: That migration will take an exclusive metadata lock on orders_indices for ALTER ... Could hold longer on high load. We still have the nightly backfill of orders. Suggest run index build on replica then swap. Alternatively change to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
cheng: Can we change to CONCURRENTLY? The migration's SQL is autogenerated by alembic. Leftover constraints mean CONCURRENTLY isn't trivial. If we can't change now we should pin api-service to v2.14 to avoid new code path that hits the new index.
kevin: pin sounds safer. I'll create a canary route to v2.14 during migration window and roll traffic back after. @maria can you estimate worst-case lock time and whether we need to drain writes?
maria: Worst-case exclusive lock ~4m under peak. With retries might be 6-7m. If we do concurrent approach it's ~20m but non-blocking. I prefer concurrent index build on replica -> swap. Need a backfill pause for 10m to avoid bloat.
sasha: Oncall: we can route 10% traffic to canary and hold if latency jumps. Rollback plan: if migration holds lock >10m or error, run rollback script: `./ops/rollback_migration 2026_03_add_compound_index` and revert api pin. Ops runbook: https://confluence.redwood.company/runbooks/db-migrations
deploy-bot: Canary started: instance ids i-0abc, i-0def. Migration step queued. Manual approval required to run CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
kevin: Approving concurrent path. Maria, please update migration to use CONCURRENTLY and bump alembic id. Also update release notes: 'db: create index concurrently on orders (non-blocking) — pin api-service v2.14 during window' :thumbsup:
cheng: Done. Pushed migration change and new alembic head. Tagging release 2026.03.15-db-concurrent. I pinned api-service in kube to image sha:abc123.
maria: Kicking off index build on replica now. ETA 18m. Starting with small batch: ```psql -c "CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_comp ON orders (customer_id, created_at);"```
sasha: Monitoring: replication lag 2s, canary error rate steady. If index build exceeds 30m we'll stop and reassess.
deploy-bot: Migration applied on replica. Index build progress: 35%.
kevin: Thanks team. Keep posting status. If anything fails, we revert to previous image and abort swap.
maria: Pausing orders backfill for 12m: `./scripts/pause_backfill orders_backfill` — will resume after swap.
sasha: Noted. Alert thresholds set: lock_time > 10m, error_rate > 1% will trigger rollback.
kevin: Final: once index is synced we run swap and unpin api-service. If all stable, release notes will include the index and the pin details.
deploy-bot: Migration finished on replica. Index build finished: 00:19:42 elapsed. Ready to swap when approved.
maria: Swap done. Verifying queries against new index, looking good.
cheng: Unpinned api-service, rolling traffic back from canary. :rocket:
sasha: Observability: tail latency stable, no new DB errors. Closing out.
kevin: Great job — saved the change window and avoided an outage. Leaving postmortem notes in the release doc.
thread_summary: Canary decision + switch to CONCURRENT index build to avoid locking; pin api-service during migration; rollback triggers and commands; backfill pause
